messages:
marta: Quick thread — ran a controlled comparison this morning: replay harness (production traces) vs synthetic loadgen (fixed-open-loop). Wanted to share findings on kernel selection, batching, KV priming, and autoscale behavior.

sam: nice, high-level takeaway? :eyes:  

marta: Short: replay shows better sustained throughput with fewer cold-starts, but synthetic exposes a worst-case path that triggers suboptimal kernel picks and slower scale-ups.

jules: can you paste the exact commands you ran? want to reproduce.

marta: Yep — replay harness: 
```
./replay_harness --trace s3://prod-traces/2026-03-01.gz --rate adaptive --duration 15m --warmup 2m --target qps 400
```
Synthetic: 
```
./loadgen --pattern open-loop --seq 1024 --qps 400 --duration 15m
```

leo: important that both used the same model binary + kernel selector config right?

marta: Exactly. We pinned model v2.3.1 and selector config B (heuristic=latency-pref, cap_batch=64). Also same KV cache settings (kv_warmup=on).

sam: logs? any kernel flips?

marta: Paste of selector trace (condensed): 
```
[00:01] kernel=fastgemm selected (seq<256)
[00:03] kernel=int8-fused selected (seq>=256 && throughput>300)
[00:05] kernel=fastgemm fallback (kv-miss spike)
[05:30] kernel=int8-fused chosen steady-state (replay)
[07:10] kernel=slowgpt selected (open-loop tail latency spike)
```

jules: slowgpt? that's the fallback when KV miss + high seq. Were those KV miss rates different between runs?

marta: Yes. Replay: KV hit ~92% after 90s. Synthetic: KV hit peaked at 60-70% and oscillated. We think synthetic pattern lacked prefix locality so cache churned.

leo: that explains kernel flips — cache misses increase memory ops and push selector to conservative kernel that avoids KV assumptions.

sam: how did that impact latency and p50/p95? numbers please.

marta: p50/p95/p99 (ms) for generation step only: 
- Replay: 18 / 72 / 210
- Synthetic: 22 / 145 / 980
Note: tail in synthetic correlated with cold starts and autoscale hops.

jules: autoscale hops? we saw scale-up times degrade?

marta: Yes. On dedicated pool with reserved capacity + burst credits enabled: 
- Replay triggered gradual scale-ups: average scale-up latency 42s
- Synthetic had multiple back-to-back scale events; average 115s (some >3m) because nodes filled, KV warmup delayed readiness, and burst credit exhaustion forced cold node allocation.

leo: did you instrument node readiness vs KV priming? where was the blocker?

marta: We added a small probe: container readiness became true ~15s after process up, but effective service (KV warm) took ~60-120s to reach steady hit rates. Runtime marked node available earlier which confused routing and caused requests to land on underprimed nodes.

sam: so heuristic: don't route until kv_hit_rate > 80% or after 60s whichever earlier?

jules: I'd prefer a hybrid: soft-route with portion of traffic then ramp. E.g., allow 10% traffic after readiness, ramp to 50% at 30s if kv>50%, full at 60s if kv>80%.

marta: Agreed. We tested a quick mock: gating with gradual fanout reduced tail latency in synthetic by ~45% and cut scale-up churn.

infra-bot: deploy-log: canary rollout of selector config B2 started by marta at 2026-03-15T10:12:00Z

leo: any kernel selection regressions vs previous baseline?

marta: We noticed one regression: when batch sizes oscillate quickly (20->64->8) selector sometimes kept int8-fused, but int8-fused has high fixed overhead for tiny batches -> p50 rose. Need a hysteresis for batch-size transitions.

sam: Hysteresis makes sense. add min-dwell time 30s or require 3 samples to change.

jules: Also consider batch-weighted cost function: prefer kernel if expected token-rate*batch_size > threshold. Quick heuristic reduces flip noise.

marta: On profiling: CPU sidecar contention also spikes during synthetic run; gperftools shows scheduler waits when many small batches arrive. That increases end-to-end latency beyond kernel efficiency.

leo: Did you compare continuous batching vs fixed batching in these tests?

marta: Yes — continuous batching with KV awareness performed best under replay. Fixed-batching (timeout-based) was more stable under synthetic but higher median latency. Tradeoff.

sam: Action items?

marta: 1) Add KV-warm gating on routing (soft ramp). 2) Add selector hysteresis + sample-count threshold. 3) Improve node readiness signal to account for kv_hit_rate. 4) Run a mixed synthetic pattern that mimics production prefix locality and rerun autoscale stress.

jules: I'll take #2 and #3. Sam can you own #4 (loadgen tweak) and include a 'prefix-locality' toggle?

sam: Yep. I'll create a small generator patch: toggles for prefix-repeat-percent and sequence-stickiness.

leo: I'll prototype the gating policy and simulate with replay traces.

marta: Thanks. We'll retest tomorrow morning and target a canary roll by EOD if numbers hold. :thumbsup:

sam: sounds good. saving commands and logs to /tmp/bench-2019876543/ and uploading to cluster artifacts.
